back: Incident notifications fire on incident create or update, scoped by severity and device group. Threat analytics notifications cover new intelligence reports, not your tenant's activity. Keyword: two channels.

Matches on file, path, command line, or IP and then hides, resolves, or downgrades the alert. Scope decides the blast radius — an over-broad rule silently discards real detections. Keyword: suppression scope.

front: Why incidents outnumber alerts so heavily
back: Defender XDR correlates related alerts across endpoint, identity, email, and cloud apps into one incident. Investigating at incident level is the intended workflow. Keyword: correlation.
Groups are evaluated in rank order and the first matching rule wins; Ungrouped devices sits last. Rank decides which automation level a device inherits. Keyword: first match.
No automated response, Semi (approval required for some or all folders), and Full (remediate automatically). 'Threats detected but nothing remediated' usually means Semi. Keyword: approval.
Not configured, audit, block, warn. Deploy in audit, review the reports, add exclusions, then move to block. Keyword: audit first.

Contains an attack in progress from high-confidence signals — disables an account or contains a device without analyst approval, even where the automation level would not allow it. Reversible from the Action center. Keyword: high confidence.
Where pending approvals sit and completed remediations are reviewed and undone. Reverting is often the correct response to a false positive. Keyword: approve or undo.
Reader views. Responder also manages incidents. Contributor also creates rules and workbooks. Running a playbook additionally needs Logic App Contributor. Keyword: playbook permission.

front: Analytics tier vs Data lake tier
back: Analytics is hot and interactively queryable. Data lake is cheap long-term storage queried asynchronously with KQL jobs. Keyword: cost vs latency.
Installs the Azure Monitor Agent and collects via a data collection rule — All, Common, Minimal, or a custom XPath filter for specific event IDs. Keyword: data collection rule.
Endpoints forward events to a collector server and only the collector runs an agent — the answer when agents cannot be deployed everywhere. Keyword: collector.
Syslog carries a raw message. CEF is the structured variant most firewalls and proxies emit and parses into named fields. Keyword: structured.
Resource diagnostic settings, applied across the estate with Azure Policy rather than resource by resource. Keyword: policy at scale.
Scheduled runs KQL on an interval over a lookback window. Near-real-time runs once a minute over recent data with restrictions on the query. Keyword: latency.
Correlate low-fidelity signals across products into high-fidelity multi-stage attack detections using machine learning. Keyword: multi-stage.
Event grouping decides one alert for all events or one per event. Alert grouping collapses alerts into a single incident by matching entities within a time window. Keyword: one incident per host.
Binds query columns to accounts, hosts, IPs, and files so the alert is investigable and the graph can be drawn. Without it an alert is just rows. Keyword: investigable.
An Advanced Hunting query must return Timestamp, ReportId, and an entity id column before it can be saved as a custom detection. Keyword: required columns.
Shows which techniques your active analytics rules cover and where the gaps are — coverage analysis, not detection. Keyword: gap analysis.
True positive, informational expected activity, or false positive with a determination — these verdicts feed tuning and the models that decide what fires next. Not paperwork. Keyword: feedback loop.
Find the earliest signal, follow the entities rather than the alerts, and check identity signals for lateral movement, not just endpoint ones. Keyword: follow entities.
Delivery action (delivered, junked, blocked, replaced) and delivery location (inbox, junk, quarantine, removed by ZAP) are the two that answer 'did it reach them'. Keyword: where did it land.
Retroactively acts on already-delivered mail when the verdict changes — the mechanism behind a message disappearing from an inbox after the fact. Keyword: retroactive.

front: Soft delete vs hard delete of mail
back: Soft delete moves messages to Deleted Items and is recoverable. Hard delete purges them. Both are recorded for review. Keyword: recoverable.
Safe Links rewrites URLs and checks them at click time, so protection continues after delivery. Safe Attachments detonates files in a sandbox before delivery. Keyword: click time.

front: Entra ID Protection vs Defender for Identity
back: ID Protection scores cloud identity risk and drives risk-based Conditional Access. Defender for Identity uses domain controller sensors for on-premises attacks. Keyword: cloud vs on-prem.

front: The step people forget after a password reset
back: Revoke sessions. A reset alone leaves issued refresh tokens valid, so the attacker keeps access. Keyword: revoke tokens.
Defender for Identity's view of which sensitive accounts a compromised machine exposes — the tool for scoping containment. Keyword: exposure.

front: Defender for Cloud Apps vs Defender for Cloud
back: Cloud Apps governs SaaS usage, shadow IT, and session control. Defender for Cloud protects workloads — servers, containers, storage, SQL. Keyword: SaaS vs workload.
Proxies a SaaS session in real time so a download can be blocked or a file labelled at the moment of access. Keyword: session control.
Cuts network access but permits Outlook and Teams so the user can still be contacted, while the Defender connection stays alive either way. Keyword: still reachable.
Gathers autoruns, installed programs, network connections, and prefetch into a zip for offline forensics. The answer when evidence must be preserved. Keyword: forensics.
A remote shell on the device — getfile, putfile, processes, connections, run a library script. Needs the advanced feature on, and a separate toggle for servers. Keyword: remote shell.
An automation rule is Sentinel-native — assign, tag, change severity, close, or call a playbook. A playbook is a Logic App that acts outside Sentinel. Keyword: inside vs outside.
Preserve an interesting hunting result with its query and notes, and attach it to an incident later. How a hunt becomes an investigation. Keyword: preserve.
An Audit (Premium) crucial event that answers whether an attacker actually read a mailbox rather than merely reaching it. Keyword: did they read it.
Record API calls against Microsoft Graph — the source for a malicious OAuth app or directory enumeration done through the API rather than the portal. Keyword: API-side.
Filter early and project early — every operator downstream then works on less data, and the time filter should come first. Keyword: filter first.
has matches whole terms and is indexed, so it is both faster and more precise. contains matches substrings anywhere. Keyword: whole term.
Buckets a timestamp into intervals so activity can be counted per hour or per day — how a beaconing pattern becomes visible. Keyword: time buckets.
Returns the row with the maximum value per group — the idiom for 'the most recent record per device'. Keyword: latest per entity.
Process creations with command lines and parent process — the first table for 'what did this program run'. Keyword: command line.
EmailEvents for delivery, EmailAttachmentInfo and EmailUrlInfo for the payload, EmailPostDeliveryEvents for what happened after — including ZAP. Keyword: email schema.
IdentityLogonEvents, IdentityQueryEvents, and IdentityDirectoryEvents come from Defender for Identity (on-premises). Entra sign-ins live in AADSignInEventsBeta. Keyword: which directory.
AlertInfo describes the alert; AlertEvidence joins it to the entities involved. Use both to pivot from an alert to what it touched. Keyword: join to entities.
Runs a hunting query continuously and notifies on new matches — watching a suspicion in real time without committing it to an analytics rule. Keyword: watch live.

front: Promoting a hunt to a detection
back: A reliable hunting query becomes a scheduled analytics rule in Sentinel, or a custom detection rule in Defender XDR with entity mapping and optional automated actions. Keyword: promotion.

front: Why threat analytics beats a generic feed
back: Reports are tenant-aware: each shows your affected device count, mitigations already in place, and the configurations still missing. Keyword: your exposure.
Shows what a compromised entity can reach — the accounts, devices, and resources at risk — turning one alert into a scoped containment decision. Keyword: reachability.
Asynchronous queries over the data lake tier that write results out rather than returning interactively — what makes a year-long retrospective search practical. Keyword: asynchronous.
Aggregate verbose data on a schedule into a compact table, so detail stays cheap while dashboards and rules query the small table. Keyword: pre-aggregate.
